projects.title: Email-to-Call Intake Automation
projects.summary: An intake workflow connecting inbound email to firm-specific routing, scheduled AI calling, and CasePeer. The engineering work sits between the message arriving and the resulting interaction becoming useful to the receiving team.
projects.challenge: Email intake, phone contact, scheduling, and case management have different data shapes and execution timelines. Joining them requires more than a synchronous chain of API calls: the workflow must preserve routing context and retain scheduled work beyond the lifetime of the inbound request.
approach: Receive email events through Resend and use a signed webhook as the intake boundary.
Route the intake to the appropriate firm and extract phone information for the next stage of processing.
Use durable scheduled work to coordinate AI calling through ElevenLabs and Twilio rather than relying on an in-process timer.
Connect the calling workflow to CasePeer so intake information and follow-up can reach the case-management workflow.
projects.outcome: A connected intake workflow that carries firm-specific context from inbound email through scheduled AI calling to CasePeer, bringing intake processing and case-management follow-up into the same integration path.

projects.title: Signals: Prospect Context & Introductions
projects.summary: Prospect enrichment and relationship discovery organized around an ideal customer profile. Signals brings prospect context, relationship graphs, introduction links, and queues into a connected workflow.
projects.challenge: A prospect record alone does not explain why an organization is relevant or how a useful introduction might happen. The product problem is to connect enrichment with relationship context while keeping the next action visible to the person reviewing the prospect.
approach: Organize prospect enrichment around the ideal customer profile, using PhantomBuster as part of the enrichment workflow.
Represent relationship context as a graph that can support exploration of potential introduction paths.
Connect introduction links and queues so discovery can lead into an actionable review workflow.
projects.outcome: A prospecting workflow that pairs ICP-based enrichment with relationship context, introduction links, and action queues, giving reviewers a connected view of prospect relevance and potential paths to an introduction.

projects.title: Payment Channels & Reconciliation
projects.summary: Payment integration work across Telebirr, banks, and USSD flows, with callbacks and Odoo reconciliation connecting payment activity to business records.
projects.challenge: Payment initiation and payment confirmation are separate events. Provider callbacks, application records, and accounting entries need a coherent integration path, while the services handling those events need a maintainable deployment environment.
approach: Connect Telebirr, bank, and USSD payment flows through FastAPI-based integration services.
Handle payment callbacks as part of the transaction lifecycle rather than relying on a customer's browser returning to the application.
Integrate Odoo reconciliation into the broader payment workflow so payment information can be compared with business records.
Work with Nginx, Envoy, and systemd for request routing and service operation.
projects.outcome: An integration path connecting Telebirr, bank, and USSD payment activity with callback processing and Odoo reconciliation, supported by FastAPI services and Linux service infrastructure.

projects.title: Multi-Tenant Marketplace
projects.summary: A multi-tenant marketplace spanning a Next.js interface, Hono APIs, Supabase, and a deployment footprint that includes Cloudflare Workers and Docker on a VPS.
projects.challenge: A shared marketplace must serve multiple tenants without confusing who owns data or who is allowed to act on it. The full-stack challenge also includes keeping product behavior consistent across the interface, API, persistence, and deployment boundaries.
approach: Use Next.js for the product interface and Hono for API concerns within the marketplace architecture.
Work with Supabase as part of the data layer, treating tenant ownership as a central design concern.
Use Cloudflare Workers alongside Docker and VPS infrastructure across the deployment footprint.
projects.outcome: A multi-tenant marketplace bringing together the product interface, API, and Supabase data layer, with application delivery spanning Cloudflare Workers and Docker on VPS infrastructure.
flow: Response to the appropriate tenant context

projects.title: Student Information & Academic Operations
projects.summary: Consultancy work on a student-information platform spanning course registration, assessment and grade workflows, graduation processes, and academic administration. Contributions connect a Nuxt/Vue interface with Laravel APIs and supporting development tooling.
projects.challenge: Academic workflows depend on consistent rules across registration, course setup, grades, and graduation. Changes must carry those rules through both the administrative interface and the API, including validation and filtering for complex student records.
approach: Develop course-registration and academic-administration workflows across Nuxt/Vue interfaces and Laravel services.
Implement and refine validation for course setup, grade-related inputs, and graduation forms.
Normalize API filters and malformed request inputs, with focused middleware tests.
Support exports, activity logging, and local/containerized development workflows.
projects.outcome: Contributions across the academic lifecycle, from student-course registration to grade and graduation administration, with supporting API validation and development tooling. The work reflects ongoing application maintenance as well as feature delivery.

projects.title: Document Processing, Management & AI-Assisted Drafting
projects.summary: Consultancy contributions across document processing, management interfaces, and AI-assisted drafting. This combined case study brings together Python document-processing workflows and Next.js/React work on permissions, sharing, and upload experiences.
projects.challenge: Useful document software needs more than extraction or generation alone. The engineering work spans parsing source material, making it useful for drafting, and building interfaces through which people can upload, organize, share, and review documents.
approach: Build Python document-processing workflows with Flask, PDF/document parsing tools, LangChain, and ChromaDB dependencies.
Implement model-selection, summary-handling, evaluation-criteria extraction, and proposal-drafting behavior.
Develop Next.js/React management interfaces for user-permission assignment, permission-aware navigation, and document-sharing state.
Refine upload experiences, search, API integration, and application state across the document-management work.
projects.outcome: Consultancy work spanning related implementations across the document lifecycle: processing source material, supporting AI-assisted drafting, and developing the interfaces for document management, review, and sharing.

projects.title: UNHCR Operational Reporting & Case Workflows

projects.challenge: Reporting and case-management applications need to make operational records useful to different users. That requires dependable import and query behavior, understandable status and transfer workflows, and interfaces that support reporting and follow-up.
approach: Implement and refine data imports, report queries, dynamic reporting behavior, and print/export functionality.
Contribute activity logging, filtering, standard-comment interfaces, and case-status and transfer behavior.
Work across Laravel APIs and Nuxt/Vue interfaces, connecting backend records with operational workflows.
Support internal ticket communication and related application maintenance.
projects.outcome: Contributions connect operational data with reporting, case follow-up, and administrative workflows. This work was undertaken through ETM; the public case study describes engineering scope without including case records or operational data.

faqs.question: What kind of engineering work do you focus on?
faqs.answer: I focus on AI automation, payments, full-stack SaaS, and cloud delivery. I am particularly interested in systems where several services must cooperate reliably, such as turning inbound events into scheduled work or connecting a payment channel to an accounting workflow.

faqs.question: How much industry experience do you bring?
faqs.answer: I bring roughly ten years of industry experience across backend systems, full-stack applications, integrations, and infrastructure. That breadth helps me evaluate tradeoffs across the whole product rather than treating the interface, services, and deployment as separate problems.

faqs.question: How do you approach AI features?
faqs.answer: I treat the model or voice provider as one component of a larger system. The surrounding workflow needs clear inputs, durable state, controlled side effects, and a way for people to review uncertain or sensitive decisions. A convincing demo is a starting point, not the reliability model.

faqs.question: Do you work across frontend, backend, and infrastructure?
faqs.answer: Yes. My work spans product interfaces, APIs, integrations, and deployment. I prefer to follow the problem across those boundaries while keeping the implementation understandable for the team that will operate and extend it.

faqs.question: Where are you based, and how can I contact you?
faqs.answer: I am based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. Email fkadeal@open.et with the problem you are trying to solve, the current system, and the kind of engineering support you need. Please keep credentials and sensitive customer data out of the initial message.

faqs.question: How can we discuss a role or consulting engagement?
faqs.answer: Email fkadeal@open.et with a short overview of your product, the engineering challenge, and whether you are hiring for a team role or seeking consulting support. Include the current stack, expected scope, and timeline so we can discuss fit and the most useful next step.

faqs.question: What consultancy work have you delivered?
faqs.answer: My consultancy work includes student-information and academic-operations systems; document processing, management, and AI-assisted drafting; infrastructure for Hibo Megazen; and full development and infrastructure for ODA Award. Company work is attributed separately, including UNHCR operational reporting and case workflows undertaken through ETM.

faqs.question: What was your role on ODA Award?
